text: The human body on the Earths surface. <break time="0.8s" /> Experiences constant air pressure. <break time="0.8s" /> Equal to 16 to 18 tons per square meter of its body surface. <break time="0.8s" /> However. <break time="0.8s" /> This pressure is not felt. <break time="0.8s" /> Because external pressure is balanced. <break time="0.8s" /> By internal pressure in the lungs and air cavities of the body. <break time="0.8s" /> During dives. <break time="0.8s" /> In addition to atmospheric pressure. <break time="0.8s" /> The pressure of the water also acts. <break time="0.8s" /> On the human body. <break time="0.8s" /> When submerged underwater. <break time="0.8s" /> To avoid feeling the pressure of the surrounding environment. <break time="0.8s" /> It is necessary. <break time="0.8s" /> To maintain the condition of equal external and internal pressure. <break time="0.8s" /> To achieve this. <break time="0.8s" /> Air or a breathing mixture is supplied. <break time="0.8s" /> To the diver. <break time="0.8s" /> Under pressure equal to the pressure applied by the surrounding water. <break time="0.8s" /> Water pressure increases. <break time="0.8s" /> Proportionally with depth. <break time="0.8s" /> It increases by 1 bar. <break time="0.8s" /> For every 10 meters. <break time="0.8s" /> It follows. <break time="0.8s" /> That a diver at a depth of 10 meters. <break time="0.8s" /> Experiences a pressure of 2 bar. <break time="0.8s" /> And to stabilize pressure. <break time="0.8s" /> The supply of a breathing mixture under a pressure of 2 atmospheres. <break time="0.8s" /> Is required.
